claim: CONFIRMED (with refinement): Fork 4's "after the harvest is verified in the registry" names no machine-checkable mechanism (no commit SHA, no manifest reconciliation), and given Fork 5's git-pull transport (zklw canonical/merges/commits; "the Mac pulls through git"), a per-repo sweep can run on a machine whose local registry clone is behind the merge commit that captured that repo's content. The prior finding's "losing the only copy" framing is not an overstatement: Fork 5's own rationale (122-123) states "the registry is the only copy" once piles are deleted, directly contradicting Fork 4's own claim two sections earlier that "Git history + the registry are the archive" (line 84). The document is internally inconsistent about whether git history is a real safety net post-prune.

'High embedding similarity' is the entire specification of the boundary that decides whether a harvested lens becomes its own registry entry or is folded behind someone else's canonical head -- no numeric value, no uncertainty, no known-answer pair set anywhere in the record, despite gating the prune's precondition.

The design correctly distinguishes null from zero hit-rate, but nothing states whether the sample size (upheld+refuted) travels with the ratio into canonical-head selection or reuse-ranking, so a 1-sample 100% cluster and a 39-sample 97.5% cluster could look identical to a selector comparing bare ratios.

A base lens's genuine 'parents: []' (verified in this repo's own melange record) is byte-identical to what a lens with lost lineage (uncommitted melange record, deleted worktree) would produce once harvested, because the design carries only the parents field forward, never the melange record's kind, so the stemma cannot distinguish confirmed independence from unknown lineage.

Reuse-before-regenerate optimizes for serving proven, high-hit-rate lenses, which pulls against flux-melange's own STEER-WIDE targeting mode whose purpose is to widen semantic distance toward novelty — over many runs this can quietly narrow the lens roster's diversity.

record_reuse's fallback destination (used exactly when the registry root can't be found or written) sits inside `.claude/flux-gen-specs/`, the same directory Stage G's prune sweep deletes from every pruned repo; the plan's own wording for what gets deleted there is ambiguous between a directory-level delete and a per-spec-file predicate, and under either reading reuse-log.jsonl's fate is undefined, while no task ever aggregates or reports a reuse rate from it.

claim: The accepted fallback's middle tier ('zklw's Ollama over Tailscale') depends on the exact network path Fork 5's own rejected-alternative reasoning names as the cause of a months-long silent 404 ('fails closed whenever Tailscale drops'), and nothing in the accepted design states that a tier-2-to-tier-3 fallthrough is logged, counted, or alerted -- the same failure class, relocated one tier down.

The hit-rate formula handles the zero-data case (null, never 0) but specifies no confidence weighting or minimum-sample floor for sparse-but-nonzero cases, so a 1/1 lens (100%) would outrank a 34/40 lens (85%) under naive ranking.

The prior finding (harvest-time embedding match, no query-time re-validation against the current target) is refuted on its literal mechanism — the design does specify a query-time embedding pipeline and the codebase's search_lenses tool already re-embeds free text per call — but the underlying risk is confirmed and worse than stated: no edge or tool call in the document actually wires a live review target to any candidate lens. The one integration point named ('the existing combine/contrast seam') resolves to combine_lenses, which takes lens names and does no embedding or target comparison at all.

Position 2 is correct and holds: position 1's literal mechanism (harvest-time embedding match, no query-time re-validation) is refuted by Fork 5's query-time embedding pipeline and by search_lenses genuinely re-embedding free text per call, but the underlying risk is confirmed and sharpened — the brainstorm names exactly one integration point for reuse-before-regenerate ('the existing combine/contrast seam'), and that phrase resolves in this codebase to combine_lenses, a tool that takes an array of lens names, string-matches them, and performs no embedding or target comparison whatsoever. No edge type in Fork 2 (embodies, variant-of, fused-from) connects a live review target to a candidate generated lens either. So the real gap, independently re-verified, is an absent match step, not a stale one.

Position 2 (absent match step) holds over the literal 'stale harvest-time match, no query-time re-validation' framing: a query-time embedding pipeline exists at the infrastructure level (Fork 5's local-Ollama/zklw-Ollama/lexical fallback chain, and search_lenses genuinely embeds free text per call), but the brainstorm names exactly one integration point for reuse-before-regenerate — 'the existing combine/contrast seam' — and that resolves in the live codebase to combine_lenses, which takes a caller-supplied array of lens names and does string lookup only, with no embedding call, no query text, and no 'current review target' object anywhere in its handler. As the brainstorm is written, reuse-before-regenerate has zero described match mechanism: an absent step, not a stale one.
